system_overview: This specification models a parameterized reliable broadcast protocol by message diffusion with crash failures, based on the algorithm described in Figure 4 of Chandra and Toueg's 1996 paper on unreliable failure detectors. The protocol ensures that if a correct process broadcasts a message, all correct processes eventually accept it, and if no correct process broadcasts, no correct process accepts. Processes may crash but do not behave maliciously.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes. Some processes may crash during execution, up to a maximum of F crashes (where F is at most T, and N exceeds 2T). Crashed processes stop participating entirely. The protocol has no dedicated broadcaster; instead, the initial state of each process determines whether it has received an INIT message from an external source.
state_variables: The system tracks: the set of currently correct (non-crashed) processes, the count of crashed processes, the control location of each process (indicating whether it has not received an INIT, has received an INIT, has accepted and broadcast ECHO, or has crashed), the set of messages received by each process (pairs of sender and message type), and the set of messages sent by all correct processes.
initial_state: Initially, no process has crashed and all processes are correct. No messages have been sent and no messages have been received. Each process starts in one of two states: one indicating it received an INIT message (will broadcast), and one indicating it did not. A variant initial state is defined where no process receives the INIT message.
actions: The protocol defines the following transitions: (1) A correct process receives a subset of sent messages, updating its received set to include all messages in that subset. (2) If a correct process starts with the INIT-received state, it accepts and broadcasts an ECHO message to all processes. (3) If a correct process that started without the INIT message receives any ECHO message, it accepts and broadcasts an ECHO message to all. (4) A correct process may crash (if fewer than F have crashed so far), which removes it from the correct set and transitions it to the crashed state. Each step combines receiving messages with one of these actions.
safety_properties: Unforgeability: if no correct process broadcasts (all start without the INIT message), then no correct process ever accepts. Type safety: all state variables remain within their defined domains.
liveness_properties: Correctness: if all correct processes received the INIT message, then eventually some correct process accepts. Relay: if any correct process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept. Reliable channels: if an ECHO message is sent by a correct process, then eventually every correct process receives it.
model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. The process set is 1 through N. Only ECHO messages are used in the protocol.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined receive-and-act steps of correct processes, ensuring that enabled actions eventually occur. The model assumes clean crash failures (no Byzantine behavior). The specification requires N greater than 2T, T at least F, and F at least 0. A separate specification variant exists for checking unforgeability with the no-broadcast initial state.
